details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/setup_serena.sh:340-363 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: probe_mcp_handshake invokes mcp_handshake_probe.py without passing the configured startup timeout, so the probe can fail slow-but-valid Serena startups.
  WHY: Reviewers confirmed the probe falls back to the 15s default while the emitted Codex config uses SERENA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC, creating a false-negative preflight path.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:26-300 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: _StderrTailBuffer is mutated on the stderr reader thread while _cleanup_process() may read it after only a 1-second join, creating a race on the shared bytearray.
  WHY: If the reader thread is still draining stderr, cleanup can read partially-mutated data and produce garbled or truncated diagnostics.
- agents.md:115-122 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: SERENA_PROBE and SERENA_QUERY are emitted but are not listed in agents.md's contractual stable log prefixes.
  WHY: Workflow-log-analysis and API-hygiene tooling depend on that documented compatibility surface, so the new prefixes have no stability guarantee.
- agents.md:around line 300 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: SERENA_PROBE and SERENA_QUERY are emitted but are not listed in agents.md's contractual stable log prefixes.
  WHY: The documented contract is the compatibility surface, so future prefix changes could silently break downstream consumers.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:~249-262 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: probe_initialize skips notifications in an unbounded loop, so a verbose server can consume the entire timeout before initialize is validated.
  WHY: The probe can time out on a healthy but chatty server because it spends the deadline processing notifications instead of reaching the response.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:293-311 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: probe_initialize has no cap on consecutive notifications, so notification spam can starve handshake validation until timeout.
  WHY: A verbose or misbehaving server can keep sending notifications and prevent the initialize response from being processed before the deadline.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:322-326 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The notification-processing loop has no bound on how many notifications it will consume before waiting for an initialize response.
  WHY: A malicious or overly verbose MCP server can spend the whole timeout window on notifications and cause a false timeout.
- tests/test_mcp_handshake_probe.py et al.:all new test_*.py files | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The new Serena contract test modules are not covered by the CI/release python3 test allowlists.
  WHY: The new tests can pass locally but never run in PR gates or release validation, letting regressions evade automation.
- scripts/serena_stats_emit.py:152-162 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: main() feeds newline-terminated lines into _parse_serena_lines(), which was reviewed as if it expected splitlines-style input.
  WHY: The reviewer reported a potential mismatch on edge-formatted Codex logs where trailing newlines could affect regex matching.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:356 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: main() uses getattr(exc, "stderr_tail", "") even though ProbeError.__init__ always initializes stderr_tail.
  WHY: This is unnecessary defensive code and a maintainability issue rather than a runtime bug.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:249 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: After successful initialize validation, _cleanup_process(proc) returns stderr tail data that is discarded.
  WHY: That loses potentially useful diagnostics on successful runs, though it does not change runtime behavior.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:175-179 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: _stderr_reader_loop catches all exceptions and silently returns.
  WHY: Swallowing stderr-read failures can hide debugging signals if the reader encounters an encoding or pipe error.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/setup_serena.sh:lines 340-348 (probe_mcp_handshake function) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The probe invocation does not pass --timeout to mcp_handshake_probe.py.
  WHY: The probe falls back to its 15s default while the runtime config uses SERENA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC, so a slow-but-valid server can be rejected preflight.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:lines 35-42 ( _StderrTailBuffer class ) and lines 224-232 (_cleanup_process) | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: _StderrTailBuffer.append() mutates the bytearray on the stderr reader thread while _cleanup_process() reads it after a 1-second join timeout.
  WHY: If the reader thread is still active, cleanup can read a partially mutated buffer and produce garbled or truncated stderr diagnostics.
- agents.md:lines 121-122 (Stable log prefixes contractual list) | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new code emits SERENA_PROBE and SERENA_QUERY, but they are not registered in the contractual stable log prefix list.
  WHY: Workflow-log-analysis and API-hygiene reporting depend on those documented prefixes, so the new telemetry lines have no stability guarantee.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- agents.md (lines 115-122) | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR adds SERENA_PROBE and SERENA_QUERY telemetry prefixes, but they are not listed in agents.md's "Stable log prefixes (contractual)" section.
  WHY: Consumers relying on the stable prefix contract will not recognize these Serena telemetry lines, so future format changes could silently break analysis.
- scripts/setup_serena.sh (lines 344-347) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: probe_mcp_handshake invokes mcp_handshake_probe.py without passing --timeout.
  WHY: The probe defaults to 15 seconds while SERENA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC is typically longer, so slow-but-valid startups can fail preflight.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py (lines 322-326) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The notification loop continues reading and discarding notifications until either a response with an ID arrives or timeout expires, with no cap on how many notifications can be processed.
  WHY: A malicious or overly verbose MCP server can flood the probe with notifications and consume the entire timeout window before initialize validation completes.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py (lines 29-42 and 291-300) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: _StderrTailBuffer.append() is called from the stderr reader thread while _cleanup_process() reads text() from the main thread after only a 1-second join timeout.
  WHY: The bytearray is not thread-safe, so concurrent mutation and read can corrupt stderr tail diagnostics.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py (line 356) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: main() uses getattr(exc, "stderr_tail", "") even though ProbeError.__init__ always initializes self.stderr_tail = "".
  WHY: This is unnecessary defensive code and a maintainability issue rather than a runtime bug.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/setup_serena.sh (line ~347 in probe_mcp_handshake function) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function invokes mcp_handshake_probe.py without passing --timeout.
  WHY: The probe uses its 15s default even when SERENA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC configures a longer runtime timeout, so slow-but-valid startups can fail preflight.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py (lines ~293-311) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The while loop processes notifications with no bound on notification count, so a verbose or misbehaving server can keep sending notifications until the deadline expires.
  WHY: Continuous notifications can consume the probe timeout before the initialize response is validated, causing a false-negative timeout.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/setup_serena.sh (line ~347 in probe_mcp_handshake function, line ~360 in PR diff) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The probe invocation does not pass a --timeout argument, so it always falls back to mcp_handshake_probe.py's 15-second default.
  WHY: SERENA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC is written into ~/.codex/config.toml but never used for the preflight probe, so a slow Serena can be rejected even though the runtime config would allow it.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py (lines ~249-262, probe_initialize function) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The loop skips notifications without any counter or separate time budget, so a verbose or adversarial server can consume the remaining probe timeout.
  WHY: The probe can time out before it ever validates the initialize response, causing a false-negative on a healthy but chatty server.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py (lines 29-35 and 200-204) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _buffer is mutated by the daemon stderr_reader thread's append() while _cleanup_process() concurrently calls text() after only a 1s join on the reader thread.
  WHY: If the reader thread lags beyond 1s, text() can see a partially mutated bytearray and produce corrupt or truncated stderr_tail diagnostics.
- scripts/setup_serena.sh (lines 360-363) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: probe_mcp_handshake() invokes mcp_handshake_probe.py without --timeout=..., so the probe always uses MCP_HANDSHAKE_PROBE_TIMEOUT's default 15s regardless of SERENA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC.
  WHY: Slow-but-valid Serena startup can exceed the probe's fixed 15s even though the emitted Codex config would allow the longer timeout, causing false failure and SERENA_AVAILABLE=false.
- tests/test_mcp_handshake_probe.py et al. (new test_*.py files) | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new test modules are not executed by CI/release workflows' explicit python3 tests/... allowlists.
  WHY: The contract tests can pass locally but never run in PR gates or release validation, so regressions in these helpers can evade automation.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py (lines 304-306: while True / if _is_notification(payload): continue) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The notification loop is unbounded, so notification flooding can consume the probe timeout before initialize validation.
  WHY: A verbose or misbehaving server can DoS the probe by spending the entire timeout on notifications even if initialize would succeed immediately after.
- scripts/serena_stats_emit.py (lines 152-162: with path.open() ... _parse_serena_lines(handle)) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The main loop streams file-handle lines into _parse_serena_lines(), but that helper was reviewed as if it expected splitlines()-style input without trailing newlines.
  WHY: On edge-formatted Codex logs, trailing newlines could affect regex matching and produce parser mismatches.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===

  PROBLEM: The handshake probe does not receive the configured startup timeout.
  WHY: The inline TOML emitter write
